findings.body:
`InsecureSkipVerify: true` is set on the shared `NewClient()` transport with no environment, config, or build-tag guard. Every caller — including production — will accept any cert, enabling MITM on ledger traffic despite the "staging only" comment.

Gate this behind an explicit non-prod config (or better: trust the staging CA via `RootCAs`), and keep verification enabled by default. A comment/`TICKET-77` does not limit runtime scope.

```suggestion
		Transport: &http.Transport{
			TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS12},
		},
```

(Replace with a conditional or custom CA pool if staging truly needs special trust.)

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this unconditionally disables TLS certificate verification for every caller of `NewClient()`, which is a production-grade MITM exposure dressed as a staging workaround.

## Narrative

`internal/ledger/client.go` wires `tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: true}` into the shared HTTP client with no environment gate, build tag, or dial-time override. The comment and ticket reference acknowledge staging-only intent and a prod follow-up, but the runtime path is global: any process that constructs this client (staging, prod, local, CI) will accept any certificate, including one presented by an on-path attacker.

That breaks the core guarantee of HTTPS for ledger traffic — account balances, transfers, or whatever this client posts/fetches can be intercepted or altered without detection. A ticket in a comment does not bound the blast radius.

## Recommended fix direction

Gate the skip on an explicit staging/dev signal (env var or constructed config), keep verification on by default, and prefer shipping the staging CA into `RootCAs` over disabling verification at all. If a temporary escape hatch is unavoidable, fail closed when `ENV=production` (or equivalent) so a mis-set flag cannot reach prod.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
